comment: Versioned strategy parameters. Every assessment stores a hash of this file so Phase 3 can answer 'which thresholds produced this verdict?'. Change values via git commits, never ad hoc.

ingestion.comment: pump.fun raw launches (~tens of thousands/day) are recorded but not snapshotted/filtered — graduation to PumpSwap is the quality gate that earns the full treatment. Flip a source between lists to change policy.

snapshots.comment: Decaying cadence: dense where the action is (first minutes), sparse later. `schedule` drives price/liquidity, which come from one batched Jupiter request covering every tracked mint and cost no RPC credits. `chainStateAtSec` (authorities + concentration, 2 RPC calls) and `holdersAtSec` (1 DAS call) are per-mint and metered, so they only refresh at these ages and are carried forward in between with their real observation timestamps. holdersAtSec does NOT start at 0, and 60s was measured to be too early too: a freshly observed mint reported 2 holders at t=0 against 1404 ten minutes later, and at 60s three tokens read 7, 9 and 1 against 167, 57 and 70 roughly a minute afterwards. The count is still converging that early, so judging minHolders against it rejects tokens for an artifact. 180s is the first age we are willing to decide on; minHolders itself still needs retuning against recorded distributions. Horizon cut 3600 -> 1800 on 2026-08-16: at ~110 new tokens/hour the old cadence implied ~9.3M RPC calls/month against a 1M/month allowance.

swaps.comment: Swap recording feeds H1, which is stated as unique-buyer growth without wash signatures. Per-minute buckets run for the whole tracking window; raw per-swap rows are kept only inside the launch windows, because tracked-token swaps measured 7.1M/day and storing them all would dwarf the dataset. These four numbers are the volume dials: measured trades within 20 slots of a pump.fun launch run mean 18.7 / median 8 / p90 35 / max 194, so maxRawPerToken trims a long tail without touching the typical case. Re-measure real growth after 24h before widening anything.

quotes.comment: Execution-cost sampling (FR-A6), feeding FR-B3's expectancy-net-of-costs. sizeSol is the standard trade the whole dataset is denominated in -- changing it changes what every previously recorded cost means, so treat it as a breaking change, not a tweak. exitHorizonsMin re-prices the same position later; FR-B3 models exit cost as entry impact x2, and these rows let Phase 3 check that assumption against reality instead of inheriting it.

alerts.comment: The `thresholds` block decides what PASSES and is therefore what the dataset records: every pass gets an alerts row and FR-A6 cost quotes. This `notify` block decides only what reaches Telegram. They are deliberately separate, because alert volume is also the execution-cost sampling rate -- tightening the pass bar to quieten the phone would cut the cost dataset by the same factor, and marginal candidates are exactly the ones that teach you where the liquidity cliff is. Measured 2026-08-16 over 485 mints: the pass bar yields ~415 alerts/day, this notify bar ~52/day. These numbers come from ~4 hours of one market regime and carry NO outcome evidence -- they are a capacity choice about how many messages are readable, not a claim about expectancy. Revisit in Phase 3 against real outcomes (FR-B4).
